materials.notes: Lattice: CODATA 2018 value refers to an ideal natural-Si crystal free of impurities, in vacuum at 22.5 °C (=295.65 K, converted +273.15). Ioffe lists 5.431 A at 300 K. Thermal expansion values are Swenson's Table 2 alpha' = (1/L20)(dL/dT); 300-850 K from his fit to Roberts' data (stated accuracy ~1e-8/K), 900 and 1000 K are values he gives in parentheses as EXTRAPOLATED (1000 K perhaps accurate to 1-2%). Above 1000 K no tabulated value was opened; the Okada-Tokumaru formula (abstract read at https://www.citedrive.com/en/discovery/precise-determination-of-lattice-parameter-and-thermal-expansion-coefficient-of-silicon-between-300-and-1500-k, quote: 'where t is the absolute temperature ranging from 120 to 1500 K') is given in 'formula'. The abstract as displayed has unbalanced brackets ('α(t)=(3.725{1−exp[−5.88×10−3{(t−124)} +5.548×10−4t)×10−6 (K−1)'); I used the standard reading shown in 'formula'. Evaluated (my computation, 1e-6/K): 300 K: 2.57, 500 K: 3.59, 700 K: 3.99, 900 K: 4.19, 1100 K: 4.32, 1300 K: 4.44, 1500 K: 4.56. These agree with Swenson within ~2% (e.g. 2.57 vs 2.62 at 300 K, 4.19 vs 4.29 at 900 K). Bulk modulus: Ioffe also lists 9.8e11 dyn/cm2 in its basic table; 1e11 dyn/cm2 = 10 GPa. Phase transitions: none at ambient pressure reported in the sources consulted (high-pressure transitions not compiled). Debye temperature is Ioffe's single value; its definition (low-T calorimetric vs other) is not stated.

materials.notes: DOUBT - bulk modulus: the same Ioffe page lists 'Bulk modulus 7.5·10^11 dyn cm-2' in its basic table AND 'Bs=7.13·10^11' computed from its 300 K elastic constants (C11=12.60, C12=4.40 e11 dyn/cm2); I recorded the value consistent with the listed elastic constants (71.3 GPa); 75 GPa is the alternative. Reviewer should check against a primary ultrasonic source (e.g. McSkimin). Thermal expansion: only a single room-temperature value could be sourced; the Ioffe page does not state its temperature explicitly (T_K=300 is an assumption, value is per °C = per K). Ioffe's alpha(T) figure (Novikova 1960) only extends to ~340 K. No accessible tabulation for 300-1500 K was found (TPRC/Touloukian vol. 13 on DTIC was unreachable; Reeber & Wang, Mater. Chem. Phys. 46, 259 (1996) paywalled). Melting: Ioffe also gives 937 °C (=1210.15 K). No ambient-pressure solid-solid transitions found in the sources consulted. UPDATE (thermal expansion): alpha(T) now from Singh (1968) X-ray powder data; values are MY derivative of the published cubic a(t) fit, evaluated only for 300-800 K because the fit's valid range is not given in the abstract I could read (the Unicam camera is a high-temperature camera, but treat >~800 K as extrapolation risk). Singh gives 6.14e-6/K at 300 K, consistent with Ioffe's 5.9e-6 RT value (previous entry). Cross-check (second source, lower quality): Shaw Nan & Liu Yi-Huan, Acta Phys. Sin. 20, 699 (1964), doi:10.7498/aps.20.699, https://wulixb.iphy.ac.cn/article/doi/10.7498/aps.20.699 (English abstract read; Table 1 read from the scanned PDF): Ge (99.9999%) 0-900 °C, a_t = a0(1 + αt + βt^2 + γt^3 + δt^4) with α=5.019e-6, β=1.230e-9, γ=5.420e-12, δ=-4.000e-15, a0=5.64573 kX (t in °C). Its derivative gives 5.10 (300 K), 6.22 (500 K), 7.77 (700 K), 8.46 (800 K) - i.e. 17% lower than Singh at 300 K and 8% higher at 800 K. Secant alphas from their measured table (18-890 °C) are 5.5-8.1e-6/K over 360-740 K. The same 1964 paper's silicon data, checked against Swenson/Okada-Tokumaru, overestimate Si alpha by ~25% on average over 303-1133 K, so I did not use the 1964 numbers. Overall uncertainty of Ge alpha in 375-600 K: about ±10%. No JPCRD/NIST tabulation for Ge above RT was found; Touloukian vol. 13 on DTIC was unreachable.

materials.notes: Thermal expansion: only a single room-temperature value could be sourced (temperature not stated explicitly on the Ioffe thermal page; T_K=300 assumed). Ioffe's alpha(T) figure (Novikova 1961) only covers ~20-300 K. No accessible 300-1500 K tabulation found (DTIC GaAs thermophysical report ADA169901 and TPRC vol. 13 were unreachable - DTIC under maintenance / 403). Debye temperature: Ioffe basic table gives 360 K; the Ioffe thermal page uses theta0 = 345 K in a low-T Cp fit (Blakemore 1982). Ioffe also gives melting point 1240 °C (=1513.15 K). Elastic constants T-dependence (Ioffe, Burenkov 1973): C11=12.17-1.44e-3T, C12=5.46-0.64e-3T (1e11 dyn/cm2) for 0<T<1513 K, implying B(T) can be derived if needed. No ambient-pressure solid-solid transitions found in sources consulted. UPDATE (thermal expansion): alpha(T) now from the Franta et al. (2026) three-term Bose-Einstein fit to experimental data (Novikova below 348 K, Glazov & Pashinkin 2000 dilatometry/X-ray 392-1185 K; table rows 'Novikova α 28–348' and 'Glazov–Pashinkin α 392–1185'). Values are MY evaluation of the fit as (de/dT)/(1+e(T)); using de/dT alone (the paper's definition) changes values by <0.6%. The fit gives 5.73e-6/K at 300 K, matching Ioffe's RT value. I could not open the Glazov & Pashinkin paper itself (Springer abstract read at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02757926: 'Thermal expansion of GaAs and InAs was measured in the temperature ranges from 396 to 1149' K). The third fit term (Theta3=2203 K) is described by the authors as a phenomenological correction. Cross-check (lower quality): Shaw Nan & Liu Yi-Huan, Acta Phys. Sin. 20, 699 (1964) (https://wulixb.iphy.ac.cn/article/doi/10.7498/aps.20.699), GaAs 0-750 °C X-ray: a_t=a0(1+αt+βt^2+γt^3+δt^4), α=6.174e-6, β=0.140e-9, γ=-1.425e-12, δ=2.282e-15, a0=5.64037 kX; derivative gives 6.18 (300 K), 6.12 (500 K), 6.21 (700 K), 6.45 (800 K); secants of their measured table (23-735 °C) 5.95-6.65e-6/K. That dataset overestimates Si alpha by ~25%, so it was not used.

materials.notes: Thermal expansion values are MY evaluation of Roder et al.'s published Einstein-model fit (Table I, PDF read in full from a third-party library copy of the APS paper; DOI given in citation). Check: high-T limits a1/a = 6.2 and c1/c = 5.7 (1e-6/K) match the paper's 'αc = (5.7±0.5)×10−6 K−1 and αa = (6.2±0.4)×10−6 K−1'. Their Debye-model fit gives values within ~0.1e-6/K of these (e.g. 300 K: 4.25 a / 3.80 c). Fit parameter uncertainty ~±7%. Values limited to <=1000 K (data end at 1025 K); no sourced values 1100-1500 K. Ioffe lists constant alpha_a=5.59, alpha_c=3.17 (Qian 1996 / Maruska & Tietjen), which Roder et al. say scatter significantly. NOTE Ioffe's labels 'αort= αc' / 'α||= αa' are confusingly worded. Lattice: a and c come from different references on the Ioffe page; Ioffe also lists c=5.178 A (Qian 1996). Cross-check: Roder's fit gives a(300 K)=3.1893, c(300 K)=5.1851 A (my evaluation) - consistent. DOUBT - melting: Ioffe's 2500 °C (=2773.15 K, converted) is not an ambient-pressure value. At ambient pressure GaN decomposes into Ga + N2 before melting (JAEA page https://rdreview.jaea.go.jp/tayu/ACT04E/05/0505.htm: 'at ambient pressure GaN usually decomposes into Ga and N2 before melting'; 'high-pressure suppresses the decomposition of GaN and allows congruent melting above 6.0 GPa'). Utsumi et al., Nature Mater. 2, 735 (2003) report congruent melting ~2220 °C above 6 GPa (from search snippet of the abstract only; not opened). An ambient-pressure decomposition temperature with a source could not be verified. Treat as low confidence. Debye temperature: Ioffe gives 600 K; Roder et al. derive Debye temperatures from expansion of 868±20 K (a) and 898±24 K (c) - definitions differ. No ambient-pressure solid-solid transitions found in sources consulted (zincblende GaN is metastable, not a transition).

materials.notes: Thermal expansion: only a single room-temperature value sourced (T not stated explicitly on the Ioffe thermal page; T_K=300 assumed). Ioffe's alpha(T) figure (http://www.ioffe.ru/SVA/NSM/Semicond/InP/Figs/853.gif; curve 1 Soma et al. 1982 to ~300 K, curve 2 Glazov et al. 1977 points at ~560-950 K) shows alpha rising roughly linearly from ~4.5e-6 at ~560 K to ~7.7e-6 at ~950 K, but I did NOT record digitized numbers because they are read off a small plot and the Glazov high-T data look anomalously steep. No accessible tabulation for 300-1500 K found (Reeber & Wang, MRS Proc. 410, 211 (1996) 'Thermal expansion of beta-SiC, GaP and InP' paywalled). Ioffe lists melting point 1060 °C (=1333.15 K). Ioffe basic table also lists Bulk modulus 7.1e11 dyn/cm2. No ambient-pressure solid-solid transitions found in sources consulted. UPDATE (thermal expansion): values are a CONSTANT range-average, 4.19e-6/K, recommended by Glazov et al. (2002) for 300-910 K (linear Δl/l(T) fit, so no temperature dependence is resolved). The paper is Russian; the PDF on mathnet.ru (official archive) has an OCR text layer, quote transcribed from it. The authors attribute a kink at 910 K to a claimed second-order phase transition in InP (heat-capacity maximum at 910 K, ~376 J/mol, their refs [11,20,21]); I have not seen this confirmed elsewhere and did NOT add it to phase_transitions. Above 910 K they give 6.48e-6/K from one study only (not entered as values). CAVEAT: 4.19 is below most room-temperature single-crystal values listed in the same paper's Table 2 (e.g. 4.56±0.1 for 298-673 K X-ray, 4.38 at 310 K, 4.48 at 300 K, 5.0 Bond method 298-673 K; polycrystal X-ray 289-912 K 4.75±0.01; dilatometric 3.87 and 3.97) and below Ioffe's RT 4.60. The real alpha(T) almost certainly rises with T, so 4.19 likely underestimates alpha at 500-900 K; treat as ±15%. Ioffe's InP figure (curve 2, Glazov et al. 1977, ~560-950 K points rising to ~7.7e-6) disagrees with this later recommendation by the same lead author; not digitized.
